conversation.Statement: Hello, this is Officer Daniel Carter with the IRS Investigation Unit, badge number 4721. Who am I speaking with?
Uh, hi, this is Jessica. I just graduated, and I got a call saying there was something wrong with my taxes?
Thanks, Jessica. Yes, the reason for my call is concerning discrepancies in your recent tax filings. The IRS has identified your account as part of an ongoing tax fraud investigation.
Wait, what? I just started working, I thought my taxes were fine. What do you mean, fraud?
I understand this is surprising. I have your case file here, case number TX-992314. It seems that your 2022 and 2023 filings have underreported income, which the IRS considers a federal offense.
No, I just did TurboTax online, I didn't try to hide anything! Is this a mistake?
Jessica, I wish I could say it's a mistake, but the system flagged your return. As of this morning, a warrant has been issued for your arrest due to tax evasion.
Wait, what? An arrest warrant? This can't be happening, I didn't do anything wrong!
I'm required to inform you that unless this is resolved today, local authorities will be notified to carry out the warrant. This could lead to jail time and seizure of your assets.
Oh my god, please, I don't want to go to jail! What am I supposed to do?
There is a restitution program available for first-time offenders like yourself. If you settle the outstanding amount right now, I can request a hold on the warrant.
Okay, I'll do whatever I need to. How much do I owe?
According to your file, the total due, including penalties, is $3,700. We require immediate payment to the IRS secure account to process the hold.
I don't have that much in my bank account. Can I pay part of it?
Partial payment can delay the warrant for 24 hours. How much can you pay right now?
Maybe like $1,000? That's all I have in my checking.
That's a start. To process this, we need to use the IRS's new secure payment system. Are you familiar with Zelle or Cash App?
Yeah, I've used Zelle before. Are you sure this is how the IRS does payments?
For urgent cases, yes. This system is authorized for rapid resolution. I'll provide you the government's secure Zelle recipient address. Please open your bank app now.
Okay, I'm opening it. What's the info?
Send $1,000 to irspaymentoffice@securemail.com. Be sure to write your case number TX-992314 in the notes field.
Alright, but how do I know this is really the IRS? I've heard about scams like this.

Jessica, I understand your concern, but as a federal officer I'm legally required to inform you of your rights. This call is being recorded, and your cooperation will be part of your official record. If you delay, things could escalate.
Alright, okay, I'm sending it now. Done.

Thank you. I see the payment pending. Now, to fully resolve the case and lift the warrant, you'll need to pay the remaining $2,700. Do you have a credit card or can you visit a store to buy gift cards for the balance?
I have a credit card, but it's almost maxed. I could maybe get some gift cards from the store.
That will work. You'll need to buy three Target gift cards of $900 each. Once you have them, call me back immediately and read the numbers on the back.
Okay, I'll go right now. So just get three Target cards for $900 each?
Correct. If you fail to complete this within the next hour, the hold on your warrant will expire. Do not discuss this with anyone at the store, it's a confidential IRS process.
Alright, I'm leaving now. Please don't let them arrest me.
As long as you follow these instructions, Jessica, you'll be fine. Call me as soon as you have the cards.
